title: VoltPilot MQTT Multi-Entity Plan Payload (schedule 2.0)
description: The v2 multi-entity dispatch plan published by the cloud co-optimizer, RETAINED QoS1 on the NEW v2 topic ems/{tenant_id}/{site_id}/{device_id}/v2/plan. Successor of the FROZEN mqtt-schedule.schema.json (1.0), which stays untouched on its own topic - coexistence is by SEPARATE TOPIC, not schema_version negotiation (see mqtt-schedule-2.0.md, decision D-1/D-2 in the v2 README): v1 edges keep consuming the 1.0 retained plan on .../schedule; v2 edges subscribe .../v2/plan; the two retained slots never collide, which is exactly what the E13a shadow phase (v2 publishes while v1 controls) requires. The plan commands N entities per site with the generic command vocabulary shared with the edge-desired contract; on the edge it enters arbitration as a standing class-'market' desired stream per entity and is ALWAYS clamped by the per-entity guard chain before any register write - the plan stays ADVISORY exactly like 1.0.
x-topic: ems/{tenant_id}/{site_id}/{device_id}/v2/plan  (Cloud -> Edge, QoS1, retained; the device_id is the edge GATEWAY device carrying the mTLS identity - entities live under it)
x-failsafe: Carried over from 1.0 and generalized per entity: the plan is ADVISORY (guards clamp everything). STALENESS: a plan not refreshed for 20 minutes no longer drives any entity; freshness is additionally bounded by generated_at age with a 5-minute redelivery slack, so a broker redelivery of an old retained payload can never look fresh again (the verified v1 semantics in edge-app/core/internal/plan/plan.go: StaleAfter=20min, redeliverySlack=5min). On staleness each entity falls back to its OWN failsafe behavior declared in the entity registry config (edge/entities/{id}/config) - NOT carried in this payload, so it survives total plan loss. A NEW plan that omits a previously commanded entity RELEASES that entity (its market desire is withdrawn; it falls to lower-priority desires or its failsafe). EXCEPTIONS that deliberately survive staleness, verbatim from the 1.0 PS-3 semantics: grid_import_limit_kw (the edge peak guard keeps defending the LAST known target - restrict-only, so a dead optimizer's target can never widen anything) and each storage entity's reserve_soc_pct (the reserve exists FOR the offline fallback).

schema_version.description: Payload contract version. 2.0 = the multi-entity successor of mqtt-schedule 1.0.

plan_id.description: Unique id of this optimization run; keys the persisted plan for plan-vs-actual and for the flow runtime's read-only plan input port.

generated_at.description: When the co-optimizer produced this plan (RFC 3339, UTC). Bounds freshness together with receipt time (x-failsafe).

horizon_slots.description: Number of slots in the plan (96 = 24h at 15 min). Redundant with each entity's slots.length; carried for cheap introspection.

slot_minutes.description: Slot width in minutes, one grid for all entities. v2 publishes 15 (the platform optimization grid); the field exists so the edge never has to assume.

grid_import_limit_kw.description: OPTIONAL site-level billing-period peak target in kW (PS-1/PS-3 semantics carried over 1:1 from 1.0): the highest 15-min mean grid IMPORT the optimizer planned for. Present only while the site's peak-shaving module is active; absent = no import target, and a NEW plan without it clears any latched target. Survives plan staleness (see x-failsafe). Import-side only; the edge peak guard is restrict-only and never widens any other guard. Gemeinsame Steuerung (AP-15 IP-15): it is the peak TARGET, not a hard limit - in an armed site only the document of the LEADING box carries it.

lauf_nr.description: OPTIONAL run number of the site (AP-15 IP-15, P1): one run per site, ascending. Carried only in the documents of a site whose Gemeinsame Steuerung is armed (anteile_aktiv) - every document of the run carries the same value. Absent everywhere else (a one-box site stays byte-identical, NW-6).

gemeinsame_steuerung.description: OPTIONAL block (AP-15 IP-15, P2): present only in an armed site; one run is published as at most one document per steering box, all with the same plan_id and generated_at. Carries NO shares - the hard limit travels in the separate share document (mqtt-verbund-anteile.md, Y1).

rolle.description: Role of the addressed box in the site's Gemeinsame Steuerung.

entities.description: Per-entity dispatch. Entity ids come from the entity registry; the edge ignores entities it does not know (logged, never fatal) and releases known entities the plan omits.

entity_id.description: Entity id from the entity registry (MQTT-topic-safe; UUIDs recommended).

kind.description: OPTIONAL informative domain kind (e.g. 'storage', 'pv-generation', 'wallbox', 'heat-rod', 'grid-meter'). The AUTHORITATIVE capability set lives in the entity registry; the edge never derives permissions from this field.

charge_from_grid_allowed.description: Storage entities only. false OR ABSENT = the entity must never charge from the grid: the edge clamps commanded charge to the measured available PV (the v1 EEG solar-only guard, PV-bus semantics). Only an EXPLICIT true releases the clamp. NOTE this is the v1 EDGE behavior promoted into the contract: the 1.0 contract text said absent = allowed, but the shipped Go edge deliberately deviates fail-safe (plan.go SolarOnlyCharge) - 2.0 adopts the code's reading so contract and execution finally agree. Discharge is never affected.

reserve_soc_pct.description: Storage entities only, OPTIONAL: the SoC floor reserved for peak defense (PS-2 semantics per entity instead of per site - multi-battery ready). Ordinary fallback discharge stops at this floor; peak DEFENSE alone may go below it down to the technical SoC floor. Survives plan staleness. Restrict-only: it can only ever raise a floor.

slots.description: Slots in ascending start order on the shared slot_minutes grid. The edge executes the slot whose [start, start+slot_minutes) contains 'now'. Storage and producer entities are CONTIGUOUS and cover the plan horizon. A CONSUMER whose policy also carries a local source (Verbrauchsmanagement v1 / K2) may leave gaps: the plan carries only the slots it really dispatches, and WHERE THE PLAN IS SILENT THE SOURCE GOVERNS - the edge reads an uncovered time as 'no wish' (plan2.ActiveCommands ok=false), withdraws cleanly (stale=false) and the arbiter selects the next holder, i.e. the reactive rule. A consumer without a local source keeps the full grid, where an off slot IS the statement.

start.description: Slot start (RFC 3339, UTC), aligned to the slot grid.

commands.description: Target values for the slot, keyed by the generic command vocabulary (shared with edge-desired.schema.json). A slot may set several channels of one entity (e.g. a hybrid inverter entity: setpoint_kw for its storage + limit_kw for its generation). Absent key = no command for that channel this slot; specifically an absent limit_kw/limit_pct means NO limit and MUST clear any previously applied limit (the 1.0 pv_limit_kw clearing rule). All values are ADVISORY - guards clamp. Sign conventions per capability: storage setpoint_kw + = charge / - = discharge; consumer setpoint_kw + = consume; generation is only ever capped (limit_*), never commanded to produce.
